lines.text: A well-equipped kitchen contains a wide range of utensils, each designed for a specific task. Cutting tools are fundamental: a chef's knife handles most chopping, slicing, and dicing, while a paring knife is perfect for peeling and detailed work. A bread knife, with its serrated edge, cuts through crusty loaves without crushing them. A cutting board provides a safe surface for all knife work. For mixing and stirring, a wooden spoon is a kitchen classic, while a whisk aerates sauces and batters. A spatula flips pancakes and burgers, and a ladle serves soups and stews. Measuring tools ensure accuracy: measuring cups, measuring spoons, and kitchen scales weigh and portion ingredients precisely. Cookware includes pots (for boiling and stewing), pans (for frying and sautéing), a wok (for stir-frying), and baking trays (for oven use). A colander drains pasta and washes vegetables, while a sieve strains fine particles from liquids. Small appliances have revolutionised cooking: a blender purées soups and smoothies, a food processor chops and slices in seconds, a toaster browns bread, and a kettle boils water. A rolling pin flattens dough, a grater shreds cheese, and a peeler removes vegetable skin. Knowing these names helps you follow recipes, shop for kitchen equipment, and communicate confidently in any kitchen.
